rite.prompt: Hall says many verbose authors were wordy for the sake of concealing what?

signal:
CRYPTO.NFO                                         HALL 1.3
================================================================
The Cryptogram as a Factor in Symbolic Philosophy
Manly P. Hall · 1928 · folio p.562 · ECHO CRAFT.SYM

THESIS
  Symbol is a cipher. If you cannot count, anagram, and
  read pictures as letters, you will take a coded book for
  a rambling one.

POINTS
  * Secret alphabets, the Bacon biliteral cipher
  * Pictorial ciphers (a drawing that is also a letter)
  * Acroamatic: oral cipher, taught mouth to ear
  * Numerical and musical ciphers — gematria's cousins
  * The lost word is a cryptogram the lodge pretends to seek

SEE ALSO  bacon  tarot  hermes  hiramic
DEGREE    NEOPHYTE may read this screen
================================================================
translation:
This is Hall’s most operational chapter, and the one that licenses the board. He says the modern world remembers ciphers as a military toy and forgets they were how philosophers hid a second book inside a first. Verbose writers were not always drunk. Sometimes they were padding to conceal words.

He lists the toolbox: secret alphabets; Bacon’s biliteral cipher (two typefaces as 0 and 1, decades before computers); pictures that are letters; acroamatic teaching (the cipher is not on the page, it is in how you were told to read the page); numbers; music. The next files on Bacon and Shakespeare are this chapter’s lab notes.

Read with the Hiramic legend: the lost word is not missing because someone forgot it. It is missing because it was designed as a cryptogram. Degrees on this BBS are a toy version of that. The signal is public. The translation is a key. The folio is the padded text. Gematria on Hall’s English is a numerical cipher run against the man who recommended numerical ciphers.

When we hide a biliteral in the login banner, that is not decoration. That is homework from page 562.
